instructions: Heat the oven to 450°F with a rack in the top third. Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment.
Pat the salmon dry and cut it into 4 portions. Transfer them to the baking sheet, skin side down if they have skin.

In a bowl, grate in 1 tbsp of the ginger and the 3 garlic cloves. Add the yogurt, 2 tbsp juice from the lemon, the oil, garam masala, paprika, coriander, turmeric and salt. Stir until it's a thick paste.
Spoon the marinade over the salmon and spread it over the top and sides. Leave it on the counter for 20 minutes while the oven finishes heating.
Slice the green chili and cut the rest of the lemon into wedges.
Roast the salmon for 10 to 12 minutes, until it flakes when you press the thickest part with a fork and the marinade is browned in spots. Thicker pieces take the full time.
For more char, switch the oven to broil and cook for 1 to 2 minutes. Watch it closely.
Taste a piece. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or a squeeze of the lemon.
Serve with steamed rice and the lemon wedges. Pass the green chili at the table for anyone who wants heat.
method_notes: Cup of Yum is the lead (4.8 from 141 reviews): a ginger, garlic, garam masala and turmeric rub, then very hot cooking. That version has no yogurt, so the yogurt comes from Bon Appeteach (1/2 cup for 4 fillets), which also says to cook it hot and not to pan sear because yogurt burns. My Heart Beets (4.56 from 9) agrees on 425°F and about 10 minutes. We use 450°F with a short broil for char, and swapped the lead's hot Kashmiri chili for mild paprika, with fresh chili on the side.
